agent_priors_used: Repeated prerequisite failures in the same thread are evidence the prerequisite should be repaired once or the thread parked, not that the same design should be re-run (agent prior; consistent with POLICY.md but not itself a SPIDER experimental result).

A treatment cannot demonstrate an advantage against a comparator that is already at ceiling; dynamic range must be certified before an execute cycle is funded (agent prior; SPIDER evidence independently supports this via EXP-PRODUCT-37989728440 and EXP-PRODUCT-37982016598).

Autonomous research systems drift toward local attractors and path dependence, so a lane's next step should be re-derived from the whole state rather than inherited by inertia (agent prior; SPIDER's own portfolio audit records this as a failure mode).
When a single measurement/execution substrate is a shared prerequisite across lanes, repairing it once has higher expected value than each lane rediscovering its absence (agent prior).

Designing a decisive two-sided falsifier with a bounded sampling frame is itself scientific work, and a loud pre-freeze DESIGN failure is cheaper and more informative than an invalid frozen measurement (agent prior).

allocation.question: On credential-free, server-rendered, no-JavaScript GET-only anchors, is a value-only-rotation (D1V: STALE AND NOT structural_change AND NOT transport_change) population spanning >= 2 independent anchors constructible AT ALL such that the anchor-clustered 97.5% lower bound of the incumbent value-blind guard's false-accept differential (M-PAIRED-FA-DIFF-D1V) is non-degenerate and M-N-D1V-ANCHORS >= 2 -- either by admitting a materially different anchor population whose transport validators (ETag, Last-Modified, Cache-Control max-age, Vary, final_url) are provably independent of the rotating value, or by a principled instrument change that reclassifies transport-validator motion caused solely by the rotating value itself, with that reclassification justified structurally rather than assumed? The DESIGN must produce a pre-freeze constructibility certificate for the >=2-anchor D1V frame (the exact anchors, the per-anchor transport-change cause, and the arithmetic showing the estimator is powered), and if no such population is constructible on this substrate it must FAIL LOUDLY and return the decisive positive-control-backed bounded reason that parks the four-anchor Part II route -- so that freshness effort can then move to a broader-population guard false-accept/calibration measurement or another sub-mechanism, rather than freeze another structurally degenerate single-anchor read.
allocation.rationale: C-FRESHNESS is the 'applicability/freshness decision' link of the decisive chain and is at EXPERIMENTAL with its Part I result (extraction-defect confirmed and replicated; dual-path extraction agrees 4/4) already accepted. Its single remaining object is the incumbent value-blind guard's false-accept on value-only rotation, whose outcome directly changes a product decision: whether a value-aware freshness channel is required or the value-blind signal set is adequate. The route is currently blocked only by a population-degeneracy attribution (ANCHOR_TRANSPORT_COUPLING), which is exactly the kind of prerequisite that should be settled once with a pre-freeze certificate instead of being re-discovered as MEASUREMENT_INVALID. This is materially narrower than the parked four-anchor Part II route (re-running those anchors is already excluded) and is a genuine constructibility question with a decisive answer in both directions.

director_mandate.portfolio_assessment: SPIDER has a coherent architecture and a small set of real blockers, but still no canonical packet validates the decisive causal chain: observe -> parameterized mechanism -> executable binding in the SHIPPED treatment -> applicability/freshness decision -> real external-agent action -> lower end-to-end cost per successful partially novel task. The whole expensive flagship (C-LLM-INHERIT / C-RESIDUAL-NOVELTY / C-PRODUCT-ECON) is gated on three readiness conditions, and exactly three lanes are correctly positioned on them: Product is installing the audited parameterized carrier in src/spider (condition 1; audit blocker B1), Runtime is certifying a non-degenerate asymmetric-discovery task bank with pre-freeze arithmetic headroom (condition 2; B2), and Intel is deciding whether any credential-free/local model can drive the minimal multi-step Web task or whether the credential-free path must be closed/re-scoped (condition 3; B3). I continue all three unchanged because each removes one genuine blocker rather than funding a benchmark that cannot yet discriminate; re-dispatching them would discard sound, v2-guarded DESIGN work. The remaining three lanes are where genuine directional judgment is required. Graph is IDLE. Its last accepted result advanced C-FRESHNESS to EXPERIMENTAL (extraction-defect confirmed and replicated on four pinned anchors) but the four-anchor Part II route is structurally degenerate: value-only rotation (D1V) is transport-coupled (M-N-D1V-ANCHORS=1), so the incumbent value-blind guard's false-accept differential cannot be read. The one decisive, still-unmeasured object is whether ANY anchored D1V population is constructible on this substrate at all. I continue Graph on C-FRESHNESS but as a materially narrowed constructibility/redesign question with a mandatory pre-freeze constructibility certificate and an explicit fail-loud/park fallback, because it sits directly on the 'applicability/freshness decision' link of the chain and its outcome changes a concrete product decision (whether a value-aware freshness channel is required). I considered pivoting Graph to C-DELTA-REPAIR and rejected it for this cycle: the accepted ceiling already includes distributed single-node local repair at blast radius 1-3 (cost ratio 0.3125, contamination 0.0, repair 1.0), so the marginal value of another repair cycle is lower than the open freshness question, and the larger-scale distributed attempts have repeatedly died on the substrate rather than the mechanism. I continue Physics on the pivoted C-WEB-DYNAMICS access-barrier question, which is a materially orthogonal observable after the value-persistence axis closed as a bounded negative, and which bears on request-scheduling economics; I continue Frontier on the site-native-discovery v2 question because it decides whether shortest-path depth is a fundamental acquisition-cost barrier before path persistence is treated as a core optimization target. No lane is parked or terminated: every lane has a plausible, falsifiable, decision-changing question and none is prerequisite-blocked beyond what its own mandate already certifies pre-freeze. The dominant remaining program risk is not lack of experiments but spending execute cycles on designs whose comparators are at ceiling or whose sampling frames are empty; every mandate below carries an explicit pre-freeze certificate or fails loudly.
